name: Lamborghini 5.2 L V10 (Gallardo LP560-4, 2008-2013; same Audi/Lamborghini engine family as the Huracan and Audi R8 V10)
summary: A 90-degree V10 that fires unevenly on purpose. The earlier 5.0 L Gallardo used split crank pins for even 72-degree firing; the 5.2 went to stiffer shared pins, so the intervals alternate 90 and 54 degrees, which with unequal exhaust manifold grouping gives the harder, raspier Huracan/R8 note.

bank_angle_deg.note: Audi MediaCenter also states 90 degrees for the R8 version.

bore_mm.note: Same in the Audi 5.2 V10 FSI self-study programme.

compression_ratio.note: Lamborghini technical director Reggiani quoted by evo: up from 11.5 to 12.5. Audi quotes 12.7:1 for the later second-generation R8 version.

firing_order.note: Audi MediaCenter, for the R8's version of this engine. Numbering from Audi's self-study programme for the related S6/S8 5.2 V10 (https://www.vaglinks.com/Docs/SSP/VWUSA.COM_SSP_923603_5.2lL_V10_FSI_Engine.pdf): cylinders 1-5 on the right bank, 6-10 on the left bank; that programme prints the same firing order. No Lamborghini-published firing order was found.

crank.value: Common-pin crankshaft: the two opposite cylinders share one unsplit crank pin (five pins). Forged steel. The earlier 5.0 L Gallardo crank had split pins (18-degree offset) for even 72-degree firing; it was dropped because it was not rigid enough.
crank.note: evo, quoting Reggiani at the LP560-4 launch. Audi MediaCenter: 'designed as a common pin shaft: the rods of the pistons on the opposite side engage with a shared crank pin'. The 18-degree figure is from Audi's programme for the wet-sump S6/S8 V10, which kept split pins and fires evenly at 72 degrees.

firing_intervals_deg.note: Audi: 'alternating firing intervals of 54 and 90 degrees'. evo prints '90deg or 58deg', which does not add up (5 x (90+58) = 740) and is evidently a misprint for 54. Wikipedia and Jalopnik both give 54/90 for the 5.2 Gallardo. Why uneven: 90-degree bank with shared pins; an even V10 needs 72 degrees between firings. With the order above, the two cylinders on one pin fire 90 degrees apart (1->6, 5->10, 2->7, 3->8, 4->9) and the step to the next pin is 54 degrees (my derivation, consistent with Audi's figures).

valves_per_cylinder.note: DOHC per bank, chain driven, roller finger followers with hydraulic lash adjustment, continuously variable timing on intake and exhaust cams.

intake_duration_deg.note: Not found. Audi says all four camshafts adjust through 42 degrees of crank angle on the R8 version.

redline_rpm.note: Not found on a page opened for the LP560-4. Peak power is at 8,000 rpm.

peak_power_kw.note: 560 PS, Gallardo LP560-4. Huracan LP610-4: 449 kW at 8,250 rpm and 560 N·m at 6,500 rpm (same page).

intake_type.value: plenum: two throttle bodies, cast magnesium variable-geometry resonance intake manifold; direct injection (FSI)
intake_type.note: Wikipedia's Volkswagen Group engine list, V10 section. Later Huracan/R8 engines add port injection.

header_type.value: per bank: one three-into-one, one two-into-one, then a single pipe joining the two downstream (unequal grouping)
header_type.note: evo: 'exhaust manifolds which, on each bank, have three-into-one, two-into-one and a single pipe joining the two-into-one downstream'. Wikipedia describes it as a '2-1-2 branch' manifold per bank.

exhaust_notes.value: Exhaust flaps open with load and rpm (Audi, R8 version).

missing: a Lamborghini-published firing order (Audi's is used)

sources.what: evo magazine, March 2008, reporting Lamborghini technical director Maurizio Reggiani on the LP560-4 engine: crank change, firing intervals, compression, exhaust manifolds.
Audi MediaCenter press text on the R8 V10 (same 5.2 FSI engine family built for Lamborghini and Audi): common-pin crank, 54/90 intervals, firing order. Manufacturer.

Audi of America self-study programme 923603 for the 5.2 V10 FSI in the S6/S8 (split-pin, even-firing sister engine): cylinder numbering, 18-degree split pin, bore and stroke. Manufacturer training document on a third-party host.
English Wikipedia Lamborghini V10 page: dimensions and outputs by model.
English Wikipedia list of Volkswagen Group petrol engines, V10 section: intake, valvetrain, outputs.
Jalopnik explainer on even and odd firing; states the 5.2 Gallardo is 54/90 and the 5.0 was even 72.

name.note: Lamborghini heritage page for the LP 560-4 Coupé, the 5.2 V10 car this def is based on.

curb_kg.note: SECONDARY. carspecs.us LP560-4 manual coupe: "3,307 lbs." (1,500 kg); supercars.net 2008 page: "curb weight" "1500 kg / 3307 lbs". Lamborghini gives only dry weight, page structured data: "Dry Weight","value":"1410 kg".

gears.note: SECONDARY, read by a helper. Trim "LP560-4 2dr All-wheel Drive Coupe 6-spd manual w/OD": First "3.31", Second "2.05", Third "1.46", Fourth "1.14", Fifth "0.94", Sixth "0.78". CONFLICT: supercars.net (https://www.supercars.net/blog/2008-lamborghini-gallardo-lp560-4/) lists only five, "2.563:1, 1.850:1, 1.423:1, 1.138:1, 0.939:1". No maker ratio table found.

final_drive.note: SECONDARY, DISPUTED. carspecs.us: "3.08"; supercars.net "3.077:1". Search summaries (pages not read) give 3.6 for MotorMatchup and 4.62 for Lambocars. Check (ours): with 3.31 x 3.08, 1st reaches about 96 km/h at 8,000 rpm, against a Lambocars snippet's "Max speed 80 Km/h" for 1st; 3.6 would fit that and put 325 km/h near 7,500 rpm in 6th, against about 6,400 with 3.08. Unresolved.

wheel_radius_m.note: Estimated (ours): rolling radius taken as 98% of the unloaded radius computed from the tyre size (rim diameter / 2 + section width x aspect ratio).

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'Lamborghini Gallardo' (read 2026-11-17), infobox layout: Longitudinal, mid-engine, all-wheel-drive (Gallardo 5.0, LP 560-4 and LP 570-4).
